newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil guerrillas block Sri Lankan forces' push.
newsitem.headline: Tamil guerrillas block Sri Lankan forces' push.

text.p: Sri Lankan forces on Tuesday halted a push into the Tamil Tiger rebels' northern stronghold amid fierce guerrilla resistance on the third day of a renewed battle, military officials said.

"The LTTE's resistance is very heavy," a military officer at the Defence Ministry's Operational Headquarters, said referring to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who seek an independent homeland for minority Tamils.
"We are consolidating our defences and the offensive is not going on at the moment," he told Reuters.

The military, making their first major push against the guerrillas in more than a month, reported dominating an area near the town of Kilinochchi, the northern entry point to the Tigers' jungle territory of the Wanni.
But the military officer, who asked not to be named, said the troops, supported by air force bombers, artillery and tanks, were still several miles away from Kilinochchi.
Defence analysts said government troops tried to outflank the rebels who were well dug in at Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo.
A military spokesman said security forces killed 35 guerrillas and wounded 100 more in Monday's fighting in which 15 soldiers were also killed and 21 wounded.
This brings the army's death toll to 37 and the number of wounded to 79 in the first two days of the renewed operation.
"Army casualties are pretty high. This means the LTTE is fighting back very strongly," an Asian diplomat said.
The army has said it wants to reopen the highway connecting Jaffna and Colombo, which passes through a large swathe of rebel-held territory separating Jaffna and the mainland.
An army major said the military suffered more casualties in a guerrilla counter-attack overnight on ground troops digging in south of the road junction town of Paranthan.
Paranthan is between Kilinochchi and the Elephant Pass at the neck of the northernmost Jaffna peninsula which was recaptured by the army in April.
The rebels had ruled Jaffna for nearly a decade with their own administration, courts and police.
"The rebels attacked the military defences with mortars last night," the major said, declining to elaborate.
The military spokesman said government troops either killed or wounded more than 200 rebels on Sunday.
"Terrorist transmissions have confirmed 35 of their cadres were killed and over 100 wounded in Monday's action," he said.

The LTTE questioned the military claim. The LTTE's Voice of Tigers Radio said only 13 of its fighters were killed on Sunday and two more on Monday. "The Tigers are fighting fiercely against the forces," it said.
It was not possible to verify the conflicting claims as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.
The military spokesman said there were fresh clashes between the military and the rebels off the east coast.
"Air force helicopters and naval craft successfully engaged approaching rebel boats and destroyed about 10 of their boats south of Vettilaikerni," he said. Casualties were not known.
The military balance has remained largely unchanged since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of 1,400 men.
It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war in which the government says more than 50,000 people have died.
